notes: NCBI Bookshelf Lichen Sclerosus was reread for clinical distribution, vaginal sparing, and the specific basal-degeneration/superficial-collagen-hyalinization/lymphocytic histology used in the key.
The 2023 lichen sclerosus update in PubMed Central independently supports the characteristic upper-dermal collagen homogenization and inflammatory pattern.

NCBI Bookshelf sources were checked separately for lichen planus, psoriasis, spongiotic dermatitis, and differentiated vulvar intraepithelial neoplasia so each distractor describes a real competing histopathologic pattern.
Official USMLE Content Outline (2026) was verified at Female reproductive system — infectious, immunologic, and inflammatory disorders — lichen sclerosus.

blueprint.competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts

claim_audit.clinical_pattern: Pruritic porcelain-white atrophic/sclerotic plaques involving vulvar, perineal, and perianal skin with vaginal sparing are characteristic of lichen sclerosus.
claim_audit.key_histology: Lichen sclerosus shows basal-layer vacuolar degeneration with superficial/subepithelial collagen hyalinization or homogenization and a subjacent band-like lymphocytic inflammatory infiltrate.
claim_audit.lichen_planus_distractor: Sawtooth rete ridges, hypergranulosis, Civatte bodies, and interface lichenoid inflammation are characteristic lichen planus features rather than the superficial dermal sclerosis of lichen sclerosus.
claim_audit.psoriasis_distractor: Regular psoriasiform acanthosis, parakeratosis, elongated rete ridges, and stratum-corneum neutrophils describe psoriasis rather than lichen sclerosus.
claim_audit.spongiotic_distractor: Intercellular epidermal edema (spongiosis) is the defining reaction pattern of spongiotic/eczematous dermatitis and does not match the sclerotic interface pattern in this vignette.
claim_audit.dvin_distractor: Differentiated vulvar intraepithelial neoplasia can show basal atypia with premature maturation and parakeratosis and may arise in a chronic inflammatory background, but that neoplastic pattern is not the expected histology of the diffuse classic lichen sclerosus plaques described here.

adversarial_second_pass.independent_reconstruction: Starting without the staged key, the age, severe vulvar pruritus, porcelain-white atrophic plaques, perineal/perianal extension, and vaginal sparing strongly localize the diagnosis to lichen sclerosus. The matching histology is basal injury plus superficial dermal collagen homogenization/hyalinization with a subjacent lymphocytic infiltrate.
adversarial_second_pass.lichen_planus_attack: Vulvar lichen planus can be painful or pruritic and can show interface inflammation, but the classic porcelain-white sclerotic anogenital plaques with vaginal sparing plus superficial dermal hyalinization make lichen sclerosus the unique best fit.
adversarial_second_pass.dvin_attack: Lichen sclerosus is a recognized background in which differentiated VIN may occur, so this was the strongest adversarial alternative. The stem intentionally excludes a focal ulcer, exophytic mass, or discrete nodular/suspicious lesion and asks about the described diffuse plaques. Therefore basal atypia/premature maturation is not an equally defensible biopsy expectation.
adversarial_second_pass.psoriasis_attack: Psoriasis can involve genital skin but would not explain the porcelain-white atrophic sclerosis or the characteristic lichen sclerosus distribution/histology.
adversarial_second_pass.spongiotic_attack: Eczematous disease can be pruritic, but spongiosis is a different reaction pattern and does not account for the sclerotic atrophic plaques.
adversarial_second_pass.cueing_check: All five alternatives are histopathologic descriptions of plausible vulvar/skin differentials at comparable specificity; the key is not singled out by grammar, answer length, or repeated terminology from the lead-in.
adversarial_second_pass.unsupported_precision_check: No cancer-risk percentage, age cutoff, treatment potency/duration, biopsy threshold, or follow-up interval is asserted. Age is contextual rather than a diagnostic rule.
